title: The Wreck of Mount Kessler
premise: Riverboat captain Gideon Vasquez pulls a sealed chest from the shallows below Mount Kessler and finds it stamped with the crest of Vhaloria, a nation erased from every map twenty years ago—and his own father's name inked inside the lid. The chest's contents, a ledger of names and a forged treaty, are worth killing for: the men who drowned Vhaloria want it back, and the last living Vhalorians want it delivered over the mountains before the first snow seals the pass. Hunted by an old army friend turned bounty man, Gideon must choose between the loyalty he owes the dead and the truth that could resurrect a nation or ignite a new war. He carries the chest across Kessler's shoulder as the snows close in, burns the treaty at the summit so no one can weaponize it, and gives the ledger to the survivors—then walks back down alone, finally free of the river's debt and his father's ghost.
about_author: Gideon Thornbury is the pen name of a former barge hand who spent eleven seasons working the inland waterways before turning to writing full-time. His novels draw on the river towns, vanished borderlands, and hard-bargaining characters he met along the way.

chapters.title: The Mood of the Water
chapters.summary: Gideon Vasquez pilots his aging riverboat through low water, reading sandbars by instinct while dodging a customs launch. POV: Gideon. Establishes his restless philosophy—that stopping anywhere too long costs more than it pays—and ends with him noting something pale snagged on the gravel bar below Mount Kessler.

chapters.title: What the River Gives Up
chapters.summary: Gideon and his deckhand, young Tam Osei, drag a lead-lined chest from the shallows. Its seal belongs to Vhaloria, a country struck from maps two decades ago. POV: Gideon. The beat is uneasy curiosity curdling into dread when Gideon recognizes the crest from a childhood he never talks about.

chapters.title: A Name Inked Inside
chapters.summary: Alone at night, Gideon pries the chest open: a ledger of Vhalorian names and a folded treaty, and inside the lid, his father's signature. POV: Gideon. Flashback fragments reveal his father vanished during the Vhalorian collapse. Emotional beat: grief reopening like an old wound.

chapters.title: The Man Who Buys Silence
chapters.summary: A well-dressed stranger named Corliss offers Gideon triple season's wages to hand over the chest unopened. POV: Gideon, with a brief Corliss interlude showing he reports to someone worse. Gideon refuses without knowing why. Beat: the trap of money versus instinct.

chapters.title: Tam Asks Questions
chapters.summary: Tam has seen the seal and starts asking about Vhaloria in riverfront taverns. POV: Tam. His eagerness draws attention; a dockside thug follows him home. Gideon realizes the boy has made them both visible. Beat: protective anger and the first cost of caring.

chapters.title: Burn the Boat or Keep It
chapters.summary: Gideon weighs scuttling his boat and vanishing upriver, but the pass over Mount Kessler closes with the snows—weeks away. POV: Gideon. He decides to cross the range and deliver the ledger to surviving Vhalorians, though he tells himself it's only to be rid of it.

chapters.title: An Old Friend's Badge
chapters.summary: At the last river town, Gideon meets Sergeant Hale Brannic—his wartime comrade, now a licensed recovery agent hunting the chest. POV: alternating Gideon and Brannic. They drink together, each lying warmly. Beat: loyalty stretched thin between old affection and duty.

chapters.title: The Ledger's Living Names
chapters.summary: Gideon studies the ledger and finds names still alive: a schoolteacher, a ferryman, a woman called Maren Ostrova who signs as 'custodian.' POV: Gideon. A letter tucked in the treaty reveals his father didn't betray Vhaloria—he tried to save it. Beat: the past rewritten.

chapters.title: Fire on the Water
chapters.summary: Corliss's men torch a moored boat as a message; Tam is nearly caught in it. POV: Tam. Gideon pulls him out of the smoke and finally tells him the truth about the chest. Beat: guilt, and trust forged in fire.

chapters.title: Leaving the River Behind
chapters.summary: Gideon sells the boat cheap to a widow who needs it more than he does—a small sacrifice that hurts more than expected. POV: Gideon. They take mules toward the Kessler trailhead. Beat: severing the identity that kept him safe.

chapters.title: The Trailhead Toll
chapters.summary: Brannic waits at the trailhead with a warrant and an offer: give me the treaty, keep the ledger, walk away clean. POV: Brannic. Gideon sees his friend means it—and sees the soldiers hidden in the treeline. Beat: betrayal wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: Up Through the Timberline
chapters.summary: Gideon and Tam flee upslope through pine and scree, using river-reading instincts to pick their line. POV: Tam, awed by Gideon's skill. They lose the soldiers but gain altitude, cold, and thin air. Beat: exhilaration shadowed by exhaustion.

chapters.title: The Hermit of Kessler Saddle
chapters.summary: They shelter with Ilsa Brandt, a hermit who once served in the Vhalorian archive and recognizes the ledger on sight. POV: Ilsa. She confirms Maren Ostrova lives beyond the pass—and warns that the treaty, if it surfaces, will kill thousands. Beat: the weight of documents as weapons.

chapters.title: Snowline
chapters.summary: First snow falls early. Brannic's party gains on them; a rockslide forces Gideon to choose between speed and safety. POV: Gideon. He takes the dangerous ridge route. Beat: survival demanding more than he wants to pay.

chapters.title: Tam Falls
chapters.summary: Tam slips on ice into a crevasse shelf; Gideon goes down after him and nearly doesn't come back up. POV: alternating. They survive the night in a snow cave, Tam feverish. Beat: love made explicit at last—Gideon admits the boy is the reason he keeps going.

chapters.title: Brannic Alone
chapters.summary: Brannic catches up but finds Gideon shielding a sick boy on a ledge. POV: Brannic. Alone, he reads the pages Gideon lets him see and understands what his employers intend. Beat: his loyalty cracks against the truth.

chapters.title: The Pass Before the Snows Close
chapters.summary: A one-day weather window. Gideon carries Tam and the chest over the saddle as the storm front devours the trail behind them. POV: Gideon. Brannic appears ahead—not arresting him, but holding the rope line open. Beat: grace from an unexpected quarter.

chapters.title: Maren Ostrova
chapters.summary: Beyond the pass, a hidden valley settlement. Maren Ostrova, the custodian, receives the ledger and hears Gideon's account of his father. POV: Maren. She reveals the treaty was the forgery that justified Vhaloria's destruction. Beat: vindication and fury entwined.

chapters.title: What Survivors Would Do With Truth
chapters.summary: Settlement leaders argue: publish the treaty and demand restitution, or stay hidden. Some want Gideon to carry copies out as proof. POV: Maren. Gideon warns that paper in the wrong hands killed once already. Beat: truth as both shield and blade.

chapters.title: The Burning at the Summit
chapters.summary: Corliss's second team breaches the valley. In the chaos, Gideon climbs back toward the pass with the treaty itself and feeds it into a signal fire where no one can ever retrieve it—the ledger of names stays with the people. POV: Gideon. Beat: climax; destroying the weapon, keeping the memory.

chapters.title: Reckoning Below the Snowline
chapters.summary: Brannic turns on Corliss's men, testifying to what he read, buying the valley its silence at the price of his career and freedom. POV: Brannic. Corliss retreats empty-handed; the snows seal the pass behind everyone. Beat: justice partial but real.

chapters.title: Downriver Again
chapters.summary: Spring. Gideon buys passage on another man's boat, Tam beside him as crew, heading nowhere in particular. He stops in a river town longer than he should—because now stopping is a choice, not a fear. POV: Gideon. Beat: resolution; the river unchanged, the man changed.
